DECISIONS:

RATIONALE:
Q1: The facts show PR #5109 (#5094's fix) was merged into `claude/implement-plan-issue-5094-verify-pr-named-review-run-provenance`, not `main`. On `main`, `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19098`) still requests only `{databaseId, event, status, conclusion, displayTitle, createdAt, startedAt}` at line 19147, with no `head_branch` and no `path`. The issue asks to apply #5094's rule to every matcher and to reuse #5094's helpers, which do not exist on `main`. Option A is the only choice that delivers the rule everywhere, and the issue exists because #6147 stalled, so it should not be split again. `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` (`scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1406-1412`) already checks event, `head_branch == default` and the title-to-path pairing.
Q2: Only a real default-branch `workflow_dispatch` run can have a null `head_branch`. A spoof from a branch copy always reports its own non-empty branch, so accepting null still rejects that spoof. It also keeps the #4928 protection the sweep comment documents at `review_autofix_sweep.yml:247-251`. Option B brings back duplicate dispatches. Option C turns a normal GitHub quirk into a release hold or skipped dispatch every tick, which is the availability stall this issue is meant to remove.
Q3: A run that fails the trust rule is by definition not a trusted review run. Today `review_merge_train.sh:676-679` turns it into `unattributed_run`, which marks the listing incomplete and holds every release. That is exactly the spoof's effect. Ignoring the run removes the stall. Keeping `unattributed_run` for trusted default-branch dispatches with no PR title (`review_autofix.yml` self-dispatches) keeps today's protection for real untitled runs.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
These are the binding implementation details for the lettered picks above.
Q1 / Q2 / Q3:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` (19098-~19215). Also every other poller site that matches the `Internal: AI Review & Autofix [pr:` / `AI Review [pr:` titles against the cached `actions/runs` blob: the stall judge's `workflow_outcomes` and both empty-commit push guards' cached scans (see agents.md "Review pipeline consolidator + ledger contract"). Find them by grepping for those title literals.
    - scripts/review_merge_train.sh: `_mt_inflight_review_branches` (591-689). The `--jq` projection at 609 already returns `head_branch`, `path` and `event`; the keying jq is at 676.
    - .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml: `dispatch_pr` / `dedupe_key` / select (238-256).
    - scripts/gh_helpers.sh: `_autofix_pr_named_review_runs` (1330-1414). The strict filter is at 1409.
    - Existing tests: tests/test_review_dispatch_default_branch.py, tests/test_retrigger_default_branch_dispatch.py, tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py, tests/test_editor_changes_lost_redispatch_budget.py, tests/test_gh_helpers_list_runs_method.py, tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py, plus the existing poller, merge-train and sweep test modules.
  steps:
    - Trust predicate, identical everywhere. A run is a trusted PR-named review run when all of these hold:
      - `event == "workflow_dispatch"`;
      - `head_branch` equals the resolved default branch, or is null/empty;
      - the title and path form an exact pair: (`.github/workflows/internal-review.yml`, `Internal: AI Review & Autofix [pr:<N>]`) or (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`, `AI Review [pr:<N>]`).
      Strip any `@ref` suffix from `path` before comparing, the same way review_merge_train.sh:676 does.
    - Poller: add one memoized resolver, a new uniquely named function plus a global cache variable. Grep first to confirm both names are unused. Read the default branch with `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --jq '.default_branch'` at most once per poll process, with NO `main` fallback, and validate the result with `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`. The existing reads (for example 19698 and 25625) fall back to `main`, so they cannot be reused as they are.
      - If `DEFAULT_BRANCH` from line 25625 was resolved without the fallback, reuse that value instead. Otherwise make the dedicated read.
      - Add `headBranch: .head_branch, path: .path` to the `--jq` projection at 19147. This adds no API calls.
      - Apply the trust predicate in the `_pnr_matches` filter.
      - If the default branch is unresolvable, log `PR_NAMED_REVIEW_RUNS pr=<N> outcome=incomplete reason=default_branch_unavailable` plus a `::warning::`, and return 1. Callers already treat an incomplete listing as fail-closed (skip dispatch or push).
      - Apply the same predicate and fail-closed rule to the cached-blob matchers. If the blob lacks `head_branch` or `path` for a run, treat that run as untrusted.
    - Merge train:
      - Resolve the default branch once per process with a memoized helper and no fallback.
      - If it cannot be resolved, return 1 with `MERGE_TRAIN_RUNS_LISTING outcome=incomplete reason=default_branch_unavailable` and a warning. The existing hold applies.
      - In the 676 jq, for review-path `workflow_dispatch` runs:
        - a run that passes the trust predicate gets the key `pr:<N>`;
        - a run on the default branch (or null) whose title is not PR-named and whose path is a review wrapper keeps today's empty key, so it still produces `unattributed_run`;
        - a run on any other non-empty branch, or a run whose title and path do not pair, is dropped. It gets no key and is not counted.
      - Non-dispatch runs keep head_branch keying unchanged.
    - Sweep:
      - Read the default branch once per sweep run with no fallback, using one `gh api repos/<repo> --jq .default_branch` call unless an existing read in that job already provides it.
      - Pass it into the jq as `--arg default_branch`. Make `dispatch_pr` return a PR only for runs that pass the trust predicate. The sweep matches only the internal title today, so pair it with the `internal-review.yml` path.
      - Keep the null-`head_branch` handling: a trusted null-branch run is still kept by its `pr:<N>` key.
      - A run that fails the predicate falls back to `.head_branch` keying. That key is the attacker's branch name, which never collides with a `pr:` key, so the spoof cannot suppress a PR's dispatch.
      - If the default branch cannot be resolved, emit `::warning::` and skip all dispatches this tick. This fails closed and avoids replacing a pending review.
    - gh_helpers: change line 1409 to `.event == "workflow_dispatch" and ((.head_branch // "") == "" or .head_branch == $branch)` so it applies the Q2 null rule. Everything else stays the same: one metadata read, and a return of 1 on resolution failure.
    - Tests:
      - For each of the four matcher families (poller listing and cached-blob scans, merge train, sweep, gh_helpers), add spoof-rejection cases:
        - (a) a same-title run on a non-default branch;
        - (b) a correct title with the wrong path (for example the internal title on `ai-review.yml`, or a branch-copy path such as `review_autofix.yml`);
        - (c) a correct title and path but a non-`workflow_dispatch` event;
        - (d) an unresolvable default branch, which must fail closed;
        - (e) a null `head_branch` trusted run, which is still accepted.
      - Merge train only: a spoofed run must no longer cause `unattributed_run`, and a default-branch untitled `review_autofix.yml` dispatch still must.
      - Keep all existing caller tests passing.
    - Add a changelog fragment at `changelog.d/<issue>-review-run-matcher-provenance.md`. Update the agents.md paragraph that describes `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` and the sweep keying to name the head_branch and path checks.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "Reuse #5094's helpers (orchestrate_poll_process.sh's default-branch cache)" becomes "a new memoized default-branch resolver with no fallback, at most one read per process or run", because those helpers never reached `main`.
  equivalence_argument: This is the same trust rule and fail-closed behaviour #5094 specified, applied to every matcher on `main`. The §14 budget holds: no per-item calls, at most one default-branch read per poller tick, merge-train process or sweep run, and gh_helpers keeps its existing single read.
  reversibility: Each matcher change is a local jq or predicate edit. Reverting one file restores its previous behaviour without affecting the others. The null-branch acceptance can be tightened later by removing one disjunct.
